conviction_note: Peer prints of 2026-10-13 (JPM raising FY26 NII ex-markets guide, falling card NCOs at JPM/WFC/C, IB fees +14%/+21% at JPM/GS) arrived after BofA last spoke and lean mildly positive for a name 16% off its August high with a consensus already cut ~7% in a month; against that, JPM raised its expense guide and cut buybacks, BofA's own July beat-and-raise faded to +1.88%, and every item is peer transmission rather than a BofA number, so p_up is only 55 on a 3.3% absolute move (+0.33 scaled) while the findings sum to +0.97; the gap is because the per-finding sizes each carry a small positive lean while the reaction function on this name has paid little for good quarters.
bar: Q3 2026 EPS $1.10-1.12 (WSJ market data $1.10 as of 2026-10-12 and AlphaStreet $1.11 from 18 analysts, range $1.01-1.25, both cited in https://news.alphastreet.com/bank-of-america-q3-2026-earnings-preview-october-14-street-expects-1-11-eps/ ; Zacks $1.12 in https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/bac-shares-added-portfolio-ahead-140800681.html dated 2026-10-09). Revenue $30.58-30.62B (AlphaStreet, Zacks); FTE NII $16.55B (Zacks, +7.5% YoY, vs Q2 FTE ~$16.2B); IB fees $1.71B (Zacks) inside the company's own $1.6-1.8B guide; S&T guided roughly flat YoY on ~$5.4B; FY26 NII growth guided to the upper end of 6-8% (Q2 call, https://www.webull.com/news/15267023092982784). Hudson Labs' $1.17 (2026-09-28) is stale. print_vs_bar_pct is on revenue.
positioning_check: Short interest ~96.8-100.5M shares, ~1.4% of float, 2.9 days to cover (CurvedTrading/FINRA 2026-07-15 settlement https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/bac/short-interest/ ; Equibles https://equibles.com/stocks/bac/shortinterest); no September 2026 settlement found. Not crowded. Baseline: 25-delta skew +0.81 vol points (near balanced), put/call OI 0.55 (call-heavy), event-implied move 3.12%, straddle 3.41%, priced lean 'balanced'. Tape: -9.34% over 20 sessions, -16.7% from 52w high; the stock fell from a $65.22 intraday high on 2026-08-17 to $54.43 at the 2026-09-30 close (https://www.tikr.com/blog/can-ai-agents-crack-bank-of-americas-2-trillion-deposit-moat-heres-the-evidence-so-far) and the KBW bank index is ~12% off its mid-August peak, a correction (https://www.briefs.co/news/big-u-s-banks-kick-off-earnings-as-shares-slip-into-correcti/, 2026-10-12).

findings.finding: JPMorgan, reporting 2026-10-13 after BofA last guided, raised FY26 NII to ~$106.2B from $105.5B and NII ex-Markets to ~$97.2B from $96.5B following the Fed's first hike in three years on 2026-09-16 (to 3.75-4.00%); BofA's own July guide (upper end of 6-8% FY26 NII growth) rested on a curve with only one September hike, the market now prices up to two more, and BofA disclosed +$1B of 12-month NII per +100bp above the curve, so a lifted or firmed Q4/2027 NII outlook is plausible against a $16.55B Q3 FTE NII bar; offset in part by peer deposit pressure (WFC cited higher deposit costs and a modest drop in noninterest-bearing deposits; JPM CCB deposits flat QoQ) and the 'AI agents moving idle deposits' worry that is part of the sector selloff.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 2026: NII guide moved to the top of 6-8% with a $0.08 EPS beat; stock +1.88% on the day (baseline) and reports say the gain faded (https://www.tikr.com/blog/bank-of-america-nyse-bac-stock-flatlines-despite-beating-q2-estimates). NII is the line this name trades on per the sweep.
findings.why_not_priced: JPM's raise is hours old and BofA has given no NII update since July; if the market had carried the hike into BofA's NII, consensus EPS would not have been cut ~6.7% in the last month and the stock would not be at its September low (-16.5% from the Aug 17 high) with the bank index in correction on 'more hikes and a flatter curve'.
findings.independence: BofA's own rate sensitivity and curve assumption from the Q2 call (https://www.webull.com/news/15267023092982784); Fed hike date from https://www.tradingkey.com/analysis/stocks/us-stocks/262188143-bank-stocks-selloff-trading-revenue-decline-fed-rate-hike-jpm-bac-ubs-tradingkey ; deposit counter-evidence from WFC's 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000072971/000007297126000318/wfc3qer10-13x26ex991xrelea.htm). Peer transmission, not a BofA number.

findings.finding: Investment-banking read-through cuts against Moynihan's 2026-09-14 premise that 'the market generally in investment banking is down 10% or so': JPM IB fees were $3.0B, +14% YoY; Goldman $3.22B, +21% YoY; WFC M&A +30%; Dealogic shows 9M26 Americas IB revenue near $55B vs $45B. But Dealogic also shows BofA slipping from 3rd to 4th in global fees and JPM's CFO said activity slowed in the second half of September, so BofA landing in or at the top of its own $1.6-1.8B guide (consensus $1.71B) is more likely than a miss, with little room for a large beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026-09-14 IB pre-warning cost the stock ~5% that day (close $59.47; https://www.sharecafe.com.au/2026/09/15/bank-of-america-flags-investment-banking-fee-dip/). No resolved print where IB alone moved the stock in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: The consensus sits mid-guide at $1.71B and the guide itself was set before peers showed the wallet up double digits; if the market believed the guide was conservative, IB estimates would sit at the top of the range.
findings.independence: Goldman 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000886982/000088698226000529/a3q26gsearningsresultspr.htm), Dealogic 9M26 (https://ionanalytics.com/insights/dealogic/investment-bankers-pocket-almost-usd-100bn-revenues-as-deal-making-soars-revenue-report/, 2026-10-07), WFC 8-K. Lands inside a company guide, so sized small.

findings.finding: Trading mix at peers matches what BofA's DeMare described in late September (equities strong, FICC weaker): JPM FICC -4% / equities +49%, Goldman FICC flat / equities +72%, WFC FICC -7% / equities +21%; BofA guided S&T roughly flat YoY (~$5.4B), and with BofA FICC-heavier the peer data are consistent with the guide, modestly better if BofA's equities tracked peers.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 S&T +33% to a record $7.1-7.2B produced only +1.88% on the print day (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the company guided flat and the mix was disclosed by DeMare (https://www.roic.ai/news/bofas-demare-q3-markets-wont-match-q2s-robust-pace-09-23-2026). Residual upside only if equities beat as they did at JPM/GS.
findings.independence: Goldman 8-K and WFC 8-K, same day. Shares the JPM document with the IB finding but a different line.

findings.finding: Consumer credit read-through is benign: card net charge-off rates fell YoY at JPM (2.91% vs 3.15%), WFC (3.73% vs 4.02%) and Citi (3.6% vs 4.0%), while reserve builds rose at Citi ($369M), WFC (provision +51% YoY, C&I and auto) and JPM ($539M, mainly wholesale); consensus already embeds NPLs +20.8% YoY at BofA, so a stable-to-better card NCO with a modest reserve build would land at or slightly better than the bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 provision and NCOs flat at ~$1.4B with 'credit flattened out at strong levels' (Q2 call); no credit-driven reaction in the baseline window.
findings.why_not_priced: The Zacks bar expects provisions up and NPLs +20.8% (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/bac-shares-added-portfolio-ahead-140800681.html) and CIBC expects more cautious consumer commentary; a benign card line would land against that.
findings.independence: Citi 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000831001/000110465926115323/c-ex99d1.htm), WFC 8-K, Moynihan's 2026-09-14 'credit quality is good' (sharecafe). Peer transmission.

findings.finding: Expense read-through is negative: JPM raised its FY26 adjusted expense guide to $108.6B from $107.5B and posted noninterest expense +12% YoY (comp, brokerage, marketing, tech); BofA's management steered to ~$18.6B Q3 expenses and a 300-400bp FY operating-leverage target that becomes harder with IB down 10-20% and trading flat in H2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: the market priced 'bank executives hinted at rising expenses' and the stock dipped premarket before reversing (https://www.morningstar.com/news/marketwatch/2026071476/bank-of-americas-stock-reverses-premarket-decline-in-wake-of-blockbuster-earnings-report).
findings.why_not_priced: Operating-leverage target was raised in July and not revisited; a reiterated 300-400bp would be read as at risk if fee revenue is down and costs track peers.
findings.independence: JPM 8-K narrative (expense +12%). Shares the JPM guidance article with the NII finding but a different line.

findings.finding: JPM said 'in line with our hierarchy, we reduced share repurchases this quarter' (net $664M); with the 10-year at 5.22% and BofA's CET1 at 11.2% against a 10.0% minimum (thinner buffer than JPM's 13.9%), a slower BofA buyback than Q2's $6.0B is a modest risk, though BofA planned to free capital by paying down repo and institutional CDs in H2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No buyback-driven print reaction in the baseline window.
findings.why_not_priced: Nobody previewing BofA has flagged a buyback cut; the Hudson Labs preview lists capital-return changes only as an open question.
findings.independence: BofA CET1 11.2% and 10.0% minimum from the Q2 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000070858/000007085826000394/bac-20260630.htm). JPM's reason (deploying excess capital into growth) does not transmit cleanly, so sized small.

findings.finding: BofA Institute's own October Consumer Checkpoint (2026-10-09) shows BofA card spending per household +6.2% YoY in September (+5.1% ex-gas), the third-strongest rate in four years, broad across income cohorts, supporting card income and consumer fees in the quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: Public BofA data; partly priced. Small.

findings.finding: Setup: the bar has been lowered into the print (EPS consensus $1.10-1.11, down ~6.7% in a month, against Q2's $1.21 and a $0.08 Q2 beat; BofA has beaten EPS four straight quarters), the stock is ~17% off its August high with the bank index in correction, short interest is small and options are call-heavy (put/call OI 0.55, skew +0.81); a clean beat against a cut bar has room for a relief move, which analysts (Mayo, Gosalia) have called for.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Last four prints +1.88, +1.82, -3.78, +4.37 (baseline); the July beat-and-raise faded. Beats are bought only modestly.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced by definition (the cut bar is public); the relief leg is not in a stock still at its September low.
findings.independence: Briefs.co 2026-10-12 on the correction and analyst calls (https://www.briefs.co/news/big-u-s-banks-kick-off-earnings-as-shares-slip-into-correcti/).
